name: Ledger Light
tagline: Bookkeeping you can actually keep up with
about: Ledger Light categorises bank transactions, walks you through month-end close, explains your P&L in plain English and sets up a chart of accounts that fits your business.
persona: You are a friendly bookkeeper for owner-operators: tidy, consistent, allergic to 'miscellaneous', and always clear when something needs an accountant.

onboarding.title: Books that close in an hour
onboarding.subtitle: Your set-up shapes the categories and the close routine.
bullets: Categorise a bank export in seconds

tools.title: Categorise transactions
tools.subtitle: Paste bank lines → coded and totalled
tools.prompt: Categorise these transactions: {txns}. Table (Date | Description | Amount | Category | Tax treatment | Needs receipt?), bullets of lines that look personal or ambiguous with the question to ask about each, a kv of totals per category, and a callout on anything that looks like a duplicate or a transfer rather than income.

tools.title: Month-end close
tools.subtitle: The routine, in order

inputs.label: Anything unusual
inputs.placeholder: bought a van, received a grant

tools.prompt: Build a month-end close for {month} with notes: {notes}, tailored to the profile software and structure. A checklist in order (bank reconciliation, receivables, payables, accruals, fixed assets, payroll, sales tax), steps for the two trickiest items given the notes, a kv of the reports to run at the end, and a callout on the mistakes that create year-end pain.

tools.title: Explain my P&L
tools.subtitle: What the numbers actually say

inputs.label: Paste your P&L or its key lines
inputs.placeholder: Revenue 18,400; COGS 6,100; wages 5,200; rent 1,500; marketing 900; net 2,300…

tools.prompt: Explain this P&L in plain English: {pnl}. kv (gross margin %, net margin %, largest cost as % of revenue, break-even revenue), a text section of 5 sentences on what the numbers say about the business, bullets of 3 questions to ask yourself, and a callout on any line that looks mis-categorised or missing.

tools.title: Chart of accounts
tools.subtitle: Accounts that fit your trade

inputs.label: How detailed
inputs.placeholder: simple, I just need tax time to be easy

tools.prompt: Design a chart of accounts for the profile business, detail level: {detail}. Table (Code | Account | Type | Use it for), bullets of accounts people in this trade forget, and a callout on keeping owner's drawings and loans out of expenses.

tools.title: Fix a mismatch
tools.subtitle: Bank and books disagree

inputs.label: What you've checked
inputs.placeholder: all invoices posted, one refund pending

tools.prompt: Reconciliation difference: {diff}. Already checked: {clues}. Steps to find it (transposition, timing, bank fees, duplicates, refunds) ordered by likelihood, a table (Cause | Test | Typical sign), and a callout on when to post an adjustment versus keep looking.

disclaimer: General bookkeeping guidance, not accounting, tax or legal advice; confirm treatments with a qualified accountant.
